A1.justification: Despite the changed title and SR-to-MR renaming, both PDFs describe the same random-matrix-plus-low-rank MIL approach. Their main text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices are readable and support comparison.

before.justification: V1 reports original classification experiments on Camelyon16, TCGA-NSCLC, and TCGA-RCC, including component ablations, sensitivity studies, and attention heatmaps.

after.justification: V2 reports original classification, treatment-response, representation-geometry, ablation, and computational-cost results in the main text and appendices.

M1.justification: The frozen random branch plus nonlinear low-rank residual mapping is retained under the MR name; GELU was already used in v1. The default ABMIL integration changes from replacing V alone to replacing both U and V (v1 Appendix D.3; v2 Appendix G.4), promoting a previously tested variant. Zero initialization of W1 is newly documented, not established as a changed procedure.

E1.justification: V2 retains the three original datasets and adds two evaluated treatment-response cohorts: Boehmk ovarian cancer and Trastuzumab HER2-positive breast cancer (Table 9; Appendix G.1). These extend coverage beyond tumor detection and subtyping to clinical outcome prediction.

E2.justification: The main comparison adds FOCUS, DGRMIL, and RRTMIL, including MR-enhanced versions of the latter two, while removing CLAM/SR-CLAM. ABMIL, TransMIL, CATE, and ViLaMIL remain. The feature-extractor comparison also replaces TransMIL with CATE (v1 Tables 5/9; v2 Tables 6/12). FOCUS was cited in v1 but was not evaluated there.

E3.justification: The reported TCGA split changes from 60/15/25 to 60/20/20. V2 removes 1-shot evaluation, retains 2-shot results in Appendix Table 7, and adds 32/64-shot experiments. It adds AUPRC, specifies macro F1, and introduces geometric diagnostics, capacity-matched controls, and computation measurements under varying bag sizes. These are substantive evaluation changes, not just relocated settings.

E4.justification: V2 adds spectral, clustering, and tangent-space analyses; trainable-anchor and identity-skip ablations; a capacity-matched comparison; and analysis beyond extreme few-shot learning. It removes v1's activation-function comparison and revises initialization and rank-sensitivity studies using different backbones. The heatmap analysis is also revised and described as a 2-shot MR-CATE example, rather than the earlier SR-CLAM example.

E5.justification: V1 reports means and standard deviations from three training runs and states that methods share random seeds. V2 reports means and standard deviations across five sampled few-shot subsets/runs and mentions cross-validation folds without specifying their number. The shared-seed statement disappears; confidence intervals and significance tests are not introduced.

E6.justification: Many existing results are replaced. For example, Table 1 reports 8-shot Camelyon16 AUCs of 53.9%/88.5% for TransMIL/SR-TransMIL in v1, versus 57.5%/65.3% for TransMIL/MR-TransMIL in v2. Revised sampling protocols prevent treating this as a controlled performance decline. V2 also adds geometric measurements, AUPRC, treatment-response, capacity-matched, larger-shot, and runtime results.

T1.justification: V2 introduces mathematical definitions for spectral entropy/effective rank and tangent-space drift in Sections 3.1.2–3.1.3. The approximation theorem and random-projection, full-rank, and low-rank-product arguments largely retain v1's substance after relocation to Appendices D–F. V1's explicit SR-specific forward/backward complexity bounds are no longer stated.

C1.justification: The central contribution shifts from a parameter-efficient block suppressing overfitting and spurious features to diagnosing low-dimensional feature-manifold degradation by linear layers and preserving geometry through a random anchor. This substantially changes the abstract, introduction, and conclusion's scientific emphasis. The earlier arbitrary-approximation/no-worse-performance claim remains in Section 3.2.3 and Appendix E.

C2.justification: V2 develops a substantially expanded geometric mechanism, including spectral sharpening and interpretations of differences between CONCH, UNI, and ResNet50 representations. It qualifies geometric statistics as diagnostics rather than predictors of performance gains. Appendix I adds limitations concerning the data-independent anchor and untested slide-level foundation models such as TITAN, alongside the retained rank and placement limitations.

D1.justification: V2 supplies project-code access information and a reproducibility statement, whereas v1 mainly promises later code-related details. It newly documents residual initialization, geometric-analysis procedures, treatment-response label construction, and insertion locations for additional backbones. Core optimizer and hardware information remains; v1's explicit batch-size statement is omitted. The PDFs establish the access disclosure, not the repository's contents or functionality.

R1.justification: V2 adds a dedicated geometric deep learning and representation-analysis subsection, supported by manifold, effective-rank, and tangent-space literature. It newly positions MR relative to LoRA and prototype-based classifiers and discusses TITAN's applicability limits. Earlier boosting and extreme-learning-machine connections are removed, substantially changing the research positioning.

P1.justification: The title, abstract, introduction, contribution list, and conclusion are extensively rewritten around geometry. SR/SP terminology becomes MR/LRP, related-work sections are reorganized, geometric preliminaries are inserted, and the main approximation proof moves to the appendix. Reproducibility, acknowledgements, an appendix contents page, and an LLM-usage statement are added.

P2.justification: V2 adds geometric Figures 1, 4, and 5, redraws the architecture schematic and rank-sensitivity plots, and restructures and expands the tables. The heatmap moves from main Figure 3 to appendix Figure 6 with revised heatmaps and layout. Its original biopsy images are reused, although the caption changes the model and slide attribution from SR-CLAM/tumor049 to MR-CATE/tumor058 without explanation.

improvement.justification: V2 substantially strengthens the empirical justification: direct geometry diagnostics and capacity-matched controls address v1's lack of evidence separating the proposed mechanism from parameter reduction. Additional evaluated baselines, treatment-response tasks, and code-access information broaden validation and improve reproducibility. These gains are substantive despite remaining weaknesses: geometric diagnostics do not establish the full causal account, some blanket ablation claims exceed Table 2's results, and the retained approximation theorem does not resolve the fixed-low-rank no-loss guarantee.
